outcomes: Finds the blockading square and a suitable piece for a passed pawn
Checks that the blockading square is not attacked, above all by a pawn
Sees when attacking or winning the pawn is better than blockading it
sources: docs/curriculum-map-v1.1.md section 3 (POS.BLOCKADE: a default, not a duty)

steps.text:
A **passed pawn** has no enemy pawn in front of it on its file or a neighbouring file. A **blockade** puts a piece on the square directly in front of it, so the pawn cannot advance.
**Rule of thumb:** the default blockader is a **knight**, because it loses no strength standing in front of the pawn. A queen there tends to be driven off; the king belongs in the endgame.

steps.caption: Black to move. White's passed pawn is on d5.

line.say: The knight lands on d6, directly in front of the passed pawn. No White piece attacks it.
White supports the pawn from the side. It still cannot advance: d6 is occupied.
Black makes a waiting move. The pawn on d5 stays blockaded.

claims.statement: Nd6 is the only blockading move.
After Nd6 no White piece attacks the knight.
After the three moves the pawn on d5 is still blockaded.

steps.text:
**Rule of thumb:** a blockade works when the blockading square is **safe** and the pawn is dangerous (passed, advanced or central). Check who attacks the square, above all pawns. A piece on a square an enemy pawn attacks will simply be taken.
It is a default, not a duty: if the pawn can be won, win it. A queen can blockade when nothing can hit it.

steps.title: Same blockade, one pawn moved
steps.prompt: In the next position White's pawn stands on c5, not c3, and Black blockades again with Nd6. Is the knight safe? Predict first, then check.
Before you moved in the last positions, what did you check first: whether the passed pawn was dangerous, who attacked the blockading square, or whether the pawn could simply be won?

steps.text: **Remember.** A blockade puts a piece on the square directly in front of a passed pawn, and a knight is the default blocker. Before you blockade, check who attacks that square, above all pawns, or the piece will simply be taken. It is a default, not a duty: if the pawn can be won, win it.
